title: Tile languages: the abstractions, in Python
brief: Model what every tile language abstracts: a Pallas-style block index map, a masked tile-loop GEMM and an online softmax written against a tiny tile API, a Gluon-style register layout, and a software-pipeline schedule. The checks run on a CPU. An optional Triton softmax runs on the A100.
hints: grid_shape is ceil(array / block) in each dimension. A 10 by 20 array in 4 by 8 blocks is a 3 by 3 grid, because the last block hangs over the edge.

A BlockSpec index map returns a block index. Multiply it by the block shape to get the first element: block 2 of width 8 starts at element 16. The slice stops at min(start + block, array size), so the last block of 10 rows in blocks of 4 is rows 8 to 10.

pallas_call loops over itertools.product of the grid. For each point, slice every input with its spec, copy the part into a zero block of the full block shape, call the kernel with those blocks and a zero output block, and copy the in-bounds part of the output block back.

tile_gemm needs a mask on every load and on the store. The mask for an A tile is (rows < M) and (ks < K), and for a B tile (ks < K) and (cols < N). The fixture raises OutOfBounds when an unmasked index leaves the array. Masked loads return 0, which adds nothing to the accumulator.

online_softmax keeps a running maximum m and a running sum l. When a tile raises the maximum to m_new, multiply l by exp(m - m_new) before you add exp(tile - m_new).sum(). Load the masked tail with other=-inf, so it neither wins the maximum nor adds to the sum.

blocked_owner splits each coordinate three ways: coordinate mod size_per_thread is the register inside the thread's run, the next digit mod threads_per_warp is the lane coordinate, and the next mod warps_per_cta is the warp coordinate. Anything above is a repeat. Linearize the lane coordinates with order[0] as the fastest dimension, and do the same for warps and for registers.

pipeline_schedule(n, S): step s loads tile s while s < n and runs the MMA of tile s - (S - 1) once that index is 0 or more. There are n + S - 1 steps. A tile is resident from its load step through its MMA step, so at most S tiles are resident.

softmax_triton is the one GPU check. It needs triton and a CUDA device. On a machine without them the check is skipped with a message. The kernel is one program per row: load with mask and other=-inf, subtract tl.max, exponentiate, divide by tl.sum, store with the mask.
